residue.label: Product form versus product value
residue.description: The repository objective describes a downloadable base repository, while the value proposition describes a governed human-machine integration framework. The ontology keeps these as separate nodes; their commercial and architectural relationship is not yet decided.
residue.next_action: Decide whether the base repository is the product, a distribution form, or one product in a broader suite.

residue.label: Product realization and outcome evidence
residue.description: The HMI thesis, dynamic work-fit principle, bounded-authority principle, and useful-governance principle are committed product direction. Their outcome claims remain unvalidated: current sources do not yet prove recognition accuracy, route usefulness, task timing, burden reduction, authority-boundary legibility, proportionate gates, or preservation of agency and domain priority. Connective and IDE Ergonomics remain intended proof surfaces.
residue.next_action: Define one product proof that observes work-moment recognition, route usefulness, task-moment fit, user choice, evidence continuity, owner visibility, authority-boundary legibility, governance overhead, domain priority, and avoidable coordination burden.

residue.label: Actor model
residue.description: Human, user, teammate, work owner, domain owner, lifecycle owner, and machine are used as roles, but their stable product distinctions are not normalized.
residue.next_action: Test the three starting actor nodes against one real product journey before adding more actor kinds.

residue.label: Product value measures
residue.description: Reviewable next steps and work continuity are desired outcomes. Ergonomic burden, route usefulness, task-moment fit, authority-boundary legibility, governance overhead, and unnecessary gates are candidate observations. No current source proves customer, productivity, rework, economic, adoption, cognitive-load, or usability value.
residue.next_action: Choose one observable outcome plus agency, privacy, domain-priority, governance-overhead, unnecessary-gate, and authority-boundary countermeasures.

residue.label: Interactive Define realization
residue.description: The business ontology includes Define, bounded Language Context resolution, and their product outputs. A separate business-system bridge models the candidate DefineSession, CLI/chat wizard, persistent questions, and session state, but no resolver protocol, DomainSpec runtime projection, or implementation is accepted.
residue.next_action: Keep the existing Language business-system bridge separate, then define the accepted request/view and Definition Pack binding contracts before implementing the resolver or agent integration.

residue.label: Language Context View contract and consumer evidence
residue.description: The product meaning now requires a digest-bound Language Context View, but no accepted request schema, view schema, freshness algorithm, resolver runtime, Definition Pack binding, or evidence of correct agent use exists.
residue.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 Define product owner
residue.next_action: Design the smallest JSON request and view contracts, state the stale-source behavior, and define one negative test where an open realization or blocked use cannot be silently consumed.

residue.label: Public product wording
residue.description: The package is private. Public-safe wording exists, but publication still requires a boundary review and cannot include private product proof or DomainSpec material.
residue.next_action: Run a public-boundary scrub only when a public derivative is requested.

residue.label: DomainSpec-governed construction realization
residue.description: The product ontology now requires the D65 construction path, but no machine ConstructionBinding registry, transition validator, DomainSpec compiler admission gate, accepted system ontology, implementation binding, or conformance evidence exists.
residue.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product ontology owner plus DomainSpec v2 construction owners plus Governance owner
residue.next_action: Complete the capability-local business-ontology registration, then design the exact DomainSpec v2 source and deterministic system-ontology projection contract before implementation work.

residue.label: Craft Product Feature kind and Product Capability relationship
residue.description: The Craft Product is the immediate context for a candidate System Construction Product Feature, but Product Feature is not yet a canonical CyberAlchemy kind and must not be silently collapsed into CAV2-D67 Product Capability.
residue.owner_route: Craft Product owner plus definitions-governance plus product ontology owner
residue.next_action: Define Product Feature with formal, plain-language, and Craft domain-context voices; decide its exact relationship to Product and CAV2-D67 Product Capability; then admit or reject the candidate feature node.

residue.label: DomainSpec v2 to Craft physical and authority migration
residue.description: Craft is selected as the current name of the DomainSpec v2 Product lineage, but source directories, implementation paths, imports, consumers, documentation links, package identities, and authority bindings still use the former name.
residue.owner_route: Craft Product owner plus Craft Project owner plus DomainSpec v2 migration and authority owners
residue.next_action: Create an exact dependency-closed rename inventory and migration plan that maps every legacy path and identity to move, alias, archive, retain, or reject; preserve rollback and validate every real consumer before deleting or redirecting legacy paths.

residue.label: ARE product approval and canonical adoption
residue.description: The ARE Product now has a first-class package and candidate graph identity, but the exact successor tested candidate has not yet received product approval or canonical adoption.
residue.owner_route: Agent Reasoning Engine Product owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
residue.next_action: Freeze the exact successor candidate, present its digest and complete current product-test evidence, then request one separate product approval decision.
